**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement affirmatively rejects take-or-pay in three places:

- **§ 2.1** — "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies," with express confirmation that declining to place a further Order Form "is not a breach or shortfall."
- **§ 7.1** — bars Vendor from imposing any "platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge" not identified in the Order Form.
- **§ 12.3** — Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no "exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."

I checked the planner's candidate sections (Fees § 7, Order Forms § 4, Term § 8) plus Termination § 9 for any commitment, volume cap, or shortfall mechanic on our side and found none. Section 9.4 additionally gives us termination for convenience with a refund of prepaid Fees, so even committed Order Form volumes carry an exit — well beyond the fallback position.

Two adjacent items I deliberately did **not** flag under this rule:
- **§ 22 shortfall language** relates to audit true-ups on licensed quantities, not a purchase commitment.
- **§ 7.7** imposes 15% of annual Fees per week as "liquidated damages" for late payment — a genuinely onerous provision running against us, but it is a payment-default penalty rather than a minimum commitment. Worth routing to whichever rule covers late-payment interest/penalties.
